title: U.S. House · Colorado's 4th District
area: Eastern Plains and parts of the western Front Range of Colorado.

context.text: Incumbent Lauren Boebert advanced unopposed from the Republican primary. Eileen Laubacher defeated write-in candidate Jenna Preston 99.2%-0.8% in the Democratic primary. Boebert represented Colorado's 3rd District from 2021-2025 before moving to run in and win the 4th District in 2024.

candidates.name: Lauren Boebert
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Republican primary, unopposed
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2021; representing the 4th District since 2025)

summary.text: Lauren Boebert is the Republican incumbent for Colorado's 4th Congressional District. A restaurant owner from Rifle who previously worked in the natural gas industry, she was first elected to Congress in 2020 from the 3rd District and won the 4th District seat in 2024. She advanced from the June 30, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

background.text: Born in Altamonte Springs, Florida; lives in Rifle, Colorado.
Career experience includes working as a natural gas product technician and owning and operating Shooters Grill, a restaurant in Rifle.

First elected to the U.S. House in 2020 from Colorado's 3rd District, defeating incumbent Rep. Scott Tipton in the June 30, 2020 Republican primary and Democrat Diane Mitsch Bush in the general election, 51.4% to 45.2%.
Won re-election in the 3rd District in 2022, defeating Democrat Adam Frisch 50.1% to 49.9% after winning the Republican primary over Don Coram, 66.0% to 34.0%.
Represented the 3rd District from 2021 to 2025, then won the 4th District in November 2024 with 53.6% of the vote over Democrat Trisha Calvarese (42.0%).
Committee assignments for 2025-2026 are Oversight and Government Reform and Natural Resources, where she is vice chair of the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee.
Advanced from the June 30, 2026 Republican primary for the 4th District with 92,651 votes; no other candidate appeared on the ballot.

priorities.text: Campaign website describes support for a strong national defense, opposition to the national popular vote, and limiting the size and pay of the federal workforce.

positions.summary: Campaign website says she will not let gun rights be taken away, describing her role as securing constitutional rights.
positions.quote: I won't let them take away our guns.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee) and is Vice Chair of the Natural Resources Committee's Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: As a sitting member of Congress, detailed floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script; this entry focuses on committee roles and stated positions per the research assignment's division of labor.

summary.text: Eileen Laubacher is the Democratic nominee for Colorado's 4th Congressional District. A 1990 U.S. Naval Academy graduate, she served 34 years in the Navy, including as defense attache in New Delhi and as a National Security Council senior director, and retired as a Rear Admiral in October 2024. She says she is running to lower costs and make government work for residents.

background.text: According to her campaign, she is the daughter and granddaughter of Navy veterans and decided as a child to attend the U.S. Naval Academy.
Entered the U.S. Naval Academy in July 1986 and graduated in 1990, according to her campaign website.
Served more than seven years as a Navy intelligence officer in the United States and abroad before moving to the Navy Reserve, according to her campaign.
Deployed to Afghanistan in 2009, according to her campaign website.
Became an Admiral in 2018. Served as Senior Defense Official and Defense Attache in New Delhi, India, from 2019 to 2022, then as Senior Director for South Asia on the National Security Council.
Retired from the Navy in October 2024 after 34 years of service, according to her campaign.
Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary for Colorado's 4th District with 99.2% of the vote, according to Ballotpedia.
According to her campaign, lives in Colorado with her husband, Chris; they raised five children, whom they homeschooled, and have three grandchildren.

priorities.text: Lowering everyday costs: housing, health care, prescription drugs and the price impact of tariffs.
Strengthening rural health care, including support for rural hospitals, expanded telehealth, and reversing Medicaid cuts she attributes to Boebert.
Supporting farmers and ranchers with a long-term Farm Bill and water infrastructure investment.

positions.summary: Calls for ending tariffs she says are raising the price of fuel, fertilizer, equipment and groceries.
Proposes capping insulin costs at $35/month, allowing Medicaid to negotiate lower drug prices, and reversing Medicaid cuts she says threaten rural hospitals.
Says she believes in the right to privacy and keeping government out of personal healthcare decisions.
positions.quote: Keep the government out of your personal healthcare decisions and your doctor's office, because I believe in our right to privacy and the freedom to make our own decisions

candidates.name: Douglas Mangeris

summary.text: Douglas Mangeris is the Libertarian Party nominee for U.S. House in Colorado's 4th District. He previously appeared on the 2024 Libertarian ballot list for the district before withdrawing. Little other biographical information is publicly available.

background.text: Listed by the Libertarian Party of Colorado as its 2026 candidate for Congressional District 4.
Ballotpedia lists him among withdrawn or disqualified candidates in the 2024 race for the same district.

candidates.researchNotes: Checked Douglas Mangeris's own Ballotpedia page (https://ballotpedia.org/Douglas_Mangeris): no completed 2026 Candidate Connection survey, no campaign website found, no news coverage of his platform. Only a personal LinkedIn and an X link are listed with no accessible content.
